title: How to turn off call forwarding on any device, iPhone, Android
summary: Want to turn off call forwarding? Check out how to do it for any device, and learn a better way to manage your incoming calls.
body_text: To turn off call forwarding on most US landlines and phones, dial *73 for Verizon, *73# for AT&T, and ##21# for T-Mobile. Then wait for the confirmation tone. On an iPhone , go to Settings > Apps > Phone > Call Forwarding and toggle it off. On Android , open the Phone app > Settings > Calls > Call forwarding and turn off every option. If forwarding turned on without you setting it up, that typically means forwarding was left on by a previous user, enabled by your carrier, or switched on by a code dialed by accident. This guide walks you through the steps to turn off call forwarding so you never miss an essential call again . Then, we introduce a better alternative to call forwarding so you can provide an excellent experience for both customers and team members. How to turn off call forwarding using star codes Using star codes, turning off call forwarding is a straightforward, if tedious, process: On a landline or traditional phone Landlines are the simple case. One code works across essentially every US provider, because deactivation is a standardized vertical service code, not a carrier-specific one. Lift the handset and listen for a dial tone, so you know the line is live. Dial *73. On a rotary or pulse-dial phone, dial 1173 instead. (Some older switches accept 73# in place of *73.) Wait for the confirmation — usually two short tones — indicating forwarding is off. On a mobile phone On mobile, the code depends on your carrier, because GSM carriers and Verizon use different systems. Check if your phone has a dial tone, so you know if it’s working. Different phones have different codes to turn off call forwarding: For Verizon phones , dial *73 For AT&T phones , dial *73# For T-Mobile phones , dial ##21# For other carriers, try the universal disable call forwarding code ##002# — just keep in mind it may stop your calls from reaching voicemail. Wait for a confirmation tone, usually a few short beeps, indicating you’ve turned off call forwarding. How to turn off call forwarding on iPhones Here’s how to remove call forwarding on an iPhone : Navigate to Settings , then Apps . Select Phone . Choose Call Forwarding from the menu. Switch the Call Forwarding feature to the off position. 💡 Pro tip: If you don’t see the toggle, it could be because your carrier manages forwarding server-side. Use the carrier app or portal instead, or try the star codes for your carrier. How to turn off call forwarding on Android phones If you have call forwarding on an Android device enabled, follow these steps to turn off forwarding. These should work on Samsung Galaxy devices and other Android phones: Launch the Phone application. Select the three-dot menu in the top right corner and choose Phone Settings Choose Calls or Supplementary services. On Google Pixel phones, tap Calling accounts and select the correct SIM card. Choose Call forwarding Turn off all the options for call forwarding: Always forward Forward when busy, or when you’re on the phone Forward when unanswered, or if you reject the call or don’t pick up Forward when unreached, or when your phone is off or doesn’t have a signal 💡 Pro tip: If you’re using a dual-SIM, make sure to choose the right line when you’re setting up forwarding. Call forwarding you didn’t set up: common causes If you never turned on forwarding but your phone shows it active, there are a few usual causes. Most aren’t cause for alarm: Conditional forwarding is on by default. This is the most common reason, and it’s why forwarding seems to keep turning back on. Carriers route unanswered and busy calls to voicemail using conditional forwarding, so it registers as active whenever you check — even though you never touched it. Because it’s a default rather than a setting you added, clearing it often doesn’t stick: the carrier re-establishes the voicemail route. A previous owner or your carrier left it on. Recycled phone numbers and refurbished phones can carry over forwarding set up by the last person who had them. Carriers also occasionally leave forwarding enabled after a port, an account change, or a support call. A company phone has it set centrally. On a managed device, an IT or telecom admin can enable forwarding through a work profile or MDM policy, so it appears without you doing anything on the handset itself. It only looks like forwarding. Do Not Disturb, Focus, and Quiet Mode silence incoming calls and send them to voicemail, which feels identical to forwarding even when none is set. On Verizon, it’s also worth checking call blocking and Verizon Smart Family filters. To clear real forwarding, use the codes or in-app steps above. If you’ve already turned forwarding off and calls still divert, that’s a different problem. See what to do when call forwarding isn’t working . You might be noticing how often manual forwarding fails. Whether you set it once and forgot, inherited it from a previous owner, or never touched it at all, you usually don’t notice until a call has already routed to the wrong place. A business line shouldn’t depend on a setting you can’t see. 4 drawbacks of using call forwarding Unconditional call forwarding is a standard feature on many phone systems, but it comes with major drawbacks you should keep in mind. For example: Calls may slip through the cracks: You may forget to remove call forwarding when you no longer wish to forward calls to another phone number automatically. You might miss mission-critical calls or get a ring at night when you’re not expecting it. Manual setup: On many traditional phone systems, you may need to manually set up your call forwarding feature each time you want to forward calls to another number or device. This gets tedious fast, especially if you constantly add or remove team members to your business number . No call forwarding for specific groups: You can’t automatically forward business calls if you use one phone number for business and one for personal. Apart from not knowing how to answer the phone , this could blur the lines between your personal and professional life. Challenges with shared numbers: If multiple team members share a phone number, forwarding could limit their access to calls on the original number — and the history of their conversation with a contact. Less context equals less prepared team members, as well as awkward conversations if customers have to repeat themselves. Balancing a business phone number and a forwarding number is usually more trouble than it’s worth. Even if you remember to deactivate call forwarding, using an old phone system to manage your business could take up time from your day. A call forwarding alternative is your best bet — virtual phone numbers . Virtual phone numbers: The better alternative to call forwarding If you rely on call forwarding to share calls between different phones, you’re probably using a traditional phone system — or worse, an outdated one. To avoid the hassle of manually transferring calls — and not being able to see any of your past phone call history with a contact — a virtual phone number is the solution you need. Virtual phone numbers let you send and receive calls and messages over the internet. This means you can take your business with you anywhere with a WiFi connection. Although they provide call forwarding capability, they also offer key features to help you avoid missed calls without the need to turn on call forwarding. Here are a few ways virtual phone numbers are a better alternative to call forwarding: 1. Split responsibility for incoming calls and messages Virtual numbers enable your team to share numbers so you don’t have to forward calls to a different phone every time you leave the office. Everyone on your team can see the same calls and messages. When a customer calls, anyone on your team can answer it so you don’t miss important calls. The best part is team members can view your business’s conversation history with each customer in a shared inbox view. This means they can easily pick up where a colleague left off and get heaps of context all in the same place. Need to delegate tasks to another member of your team? Just tag them internally so you can collaborate on the perfect response. 2. Set a custom ring order for incoming calls If you have many people on your team who share the same forwarding number, it can be hard to decide who should answer the calls first. The bad news is call forwarding doesn’t allow for custom segmentation with incoming call recipients. The good news is virtual phone numbers do. Custom ring orders make it easy to segment which team members receive incoming calls first. That way, calls go to other members of your team if they go unanswered in the first couple of rings. Quo also gives you more ways to automatically route calls using conditional call forwarding . If no one on your team answers the phone, you can send callers to a backup support team or forward them to a different number during or after business hours. 3. Set business hours and let calls route themselves Stop dialing *72 to forward your line every evening and *73 to pull it back every morning. Instead, set business hours once and calls route automatically on the schedule you choose. Any callers who reach you outside business hours get sent to voicemail or receive an auto-reply , depending on your phone settings. Coming up on a vacation or a company-wide holiday? You can adjust your business hours to set expectations with customers. Quo also lets you upload a custom voicemail greeting for calls made outside of business hours, which helps customers know when they can reach you next. Team members can also set their own working hours , which makes it easier to work in shift-based schedules and ensures you have adequate support coverage. Add this to analytics , including Quo’s hotspot charts, and you can see the days with the most calls and decide who to assign during peak call volume . “Quo offers a lot more flexibility than your traditional business line. You can set your business hours and customize away messages with a few clicks. If you are looking for intuitive, clean user experiences with your VOIP business phone service, Quo is for you.” — Melissa Hughes, Principal/Owner, Halogen Design Lab What to read next Want to weigh your options beyond traditional cell carriers? See our guide to the best call forwarding apps . FAQs What are some tips if call forwarding won’t turn off? Here are a few troubleshooting tips if you can’t disable call forwarding: 1. Try these quick fixes: – Restart your phone – Try dialing the universal call forwarding deactivate code ##002# – Check WiFi or data signal strength when disabling 2. If codes don’t work: – Remove and reinsert your SIM card – Toggle airplane mode to reset the network – Use your phone carrier’s app – Contact customer service 3. Confirm call forwarding is disabled: – Make a test call – Check the settings in your phone – Listen for confirmation tones What does *73 do on Verizon? *73 is Verizon’s star code to remove unconditional call forwarding, or forwarding all calls to another number. If you’ve set up other types of call forwarding on Verizon, you’ll need to use different codes: – Call forwarding busy line: turn on *90; turn off *91 – Call forwarding busy don’t answer: turn on *92; turn off *93 Why does call forwarding keep turning back on? The cause is usually conditional call forwarding, which diverts calls only when you’re busy or don’t answer. That’s why it looks active again after each missed call. The fix most people miss: turn off every conditional option (busy, no answer, unreachable) individually, not just “always forward,” which only clears unconditional forwarding. Will turning off call forwarding affect my voicemail? Usually turning off the “always forward” setting won’t touch your voicemail. Unanswered calls just ring your phone and reach your own carrier voicemail again, instead of the forward-to number’s voicemail. The one exception: if you dial ##002#, the universal code that clears every forwarding type at once, it can stop calls from reaching your voicemail. That’s because voicemail itself runs on conditional forwarding (the busy and no-answer routes). If you only want to stop forwarding to another number, turn off unconditional forwarding and leave the conditional routes alone. How do I turn off call forwarding #62? Just dial ##62# and you’ll disable call forwarding for when your phone is unreachable or out of service. This code works on major carriers like T-Mobile and should cancel the forwarding settings. How do I turn off call forwarding on my Samsung Galaxy? Head to your Phone app, tap Settings, then Calls or Supplementary services, Call forwarding, and you’ll see options for each forwarding type that you can turn off. It’s usually just a matter of tapping each one and selecting “Disable.” How do I turn off call forwarding with *72? Since *72 ‌turns call forwarding on, you’ll want to dial *73# to turn it off instead. What are the steps to cancel call forwarding on my phone? The easiest way is to dial the right disable code like ##21# for all forwarding, restart your phone, and then make a test call to make sure everything’s working normally. Most carriers use similar codes, so these universal ones usually do the trick. What’s the difference between conditional and unconditional call forwarding? Unconditional forwarding sends all your calls to another phone right away. Conditional forwarding only works when you’re busy, don’t answer, or your phone can’t be reached. Think of conditional as your backup plan and unconditional as an all-the-time redirect. How do I check if call forwarding is active? On mobile phones, you can try dialing *#21# to see the status of unconditional forwarding, though this may not work on every carrier. You can also open your phone’s call forwarding settings. On a landline, call your number from another phone to test. Does airplane mode turn off call forwarding? No, airplane mode only disconnects your device from the network; carrier-level forwarding still diverts calls before they reach your phone. Toggling airplane mode can refresh the network so a deactivation code takes, but it doesn’t disable forwarding by itself.

title: Autonomous finance: what it means for payment infrastructure
summary: Learn how autonomous finance payment infrastructure enforces immutable postings, idempotent contracts, and traceable flows of funds.
body_text: Autonomous finance payment infrastructure must enforce correctness structurally, as payment initiation shifts to AI agents. Your AI payment agent calls a payout API, times out, and retries on its fallback path. Both requests are clear, but the ledger shows a single posting, and the payment rail shows it moved funds twice. The human-run reconciliation job that would have caught this error runs the next day, but by then, the AI payment has issued 4,000 more instructions. Autonomous finance moves payment initiation from humans to AI agents, and it turns every guarantee your ledger enforces by convention into one it must enforce by structure. What does "autonomous finance" mean? Autonomous finance is the operating model in which AI agents, rather than humans, initiate, authorize, and settle financial transactions on behalf of an organization or end user. Instead of a person clicking "approve" in a checkout flow, treasury dashboard, or maker-checker queue, an agent evaluates conditions, decides to move funds, and executes the payment against the underlying ledger and payment rails. The term covers a spectrum of agent involvement: Advisory autonomy: an agent recommends a payment or reconciliation action, and a human confirms it. Bounded autonomy: an agent executes payments within a scoped authorization envelope, such as a spending limit, counterparty allowlist, or asset class. Full autonomy: an agent creates, authorizes, and discharges obligations end-to-end, including agent-to-agent (A2A) obligations where one agent pays another for data, inference, or services. What separates autonomous finance from traditional automation is decision authority. A traditional automation rule executes a decision that a human already made, while an autonomous agent makes the decision itself at machine speed and volume. That transfer of payment-initiation authority from humans to agents is what forces every guarantee previously enforced by human review to be recorded in the ledger itself as a structural invariant. It also exposes three specific failure modes when it doesn't have the correct structure. Three failure modes in autonomous finance agents Autonomous finance agents expose three failure modes the ledger must contain: duplicate postings on retries, ledger-to-rail divergence across multi-step chains, and lost attribution inside pooled omnibus accounts. Each is a variant of the same underlying pattern: what we call the retry-into-a-broken-invariant cascade . This is when an agent retries or continues a workflow against a ledger that does not structurally enforce the relevant invariant, and the resulting error is amplified at machine cadence before any human review can intercept it. 1. Duplicate postings on agent retries An agent retrying a timed-out payment call will generate duplicate postings in any ledger that relies on humans to catch and reverse double-sends. For any endpoint that charges money, accidentally calling it twice can double-charge the customer. Human-cadence systems already fail this way. On Christmas Day 2021, a scheduling issue at Santander UK caused payments from roughly 2,000 business accounts to be processed twice. The issue deposited £130 million into about 75,000 accounts in error because the duplicates landed at rival banks. Santander had to request their retrieval from dozens of other institutions. Agents retry in milliseconds, across fallback paths, at volumes no reconciliation cadence can absorb after the fact. 2. Ledger-to-rail divergence across multi-step agent chains Splitting authorization, execution, and settlement across separate agent steps causes the ledger state to diverge from the rail state the moment any intermediate step fails mid-chain. Multi-step chains without distributed transactions typically use the saga pattern, and its limitation is that compensating transactions must be designed explicitly, while concurrent sagas can lose isolation. Common failure cases include client timeouts after a successful call, delayed provider callbacks, duplicate webhooks, a worker crashing after the database commit, and a refund succeeding externally while the internal update fails. Each of these failures leaves the ledger asserting a state the rail never reached, or vice versa. Ledger-rail drifts stay invisible until automated reconciliation runs, and an agent chain will have executed thousands more steps on top of the divergent state by then. 3. Lost attribution inside omnibus accounts Autonomous fund movement across pooled omnibus accounts destroys per-agent, per-action attribution unless the ledger tags obligations at the sub-account level. When a fintech pools end-user funds in a single for-benefit-of (FBO) account at a partner bank, the bank sees a single balance, and the fintech's sub-ledger must track each user's share. Without a per-beneficiary posting for every transfer, no one can answer who owned what at a given moment, which is a record that Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) pass-through insurance explicitly requires to be identifiable in the bank's records. When agents move funds through the pool, the ledger must record which agent moved which funds for whom at the time of posting. Four ledger invariants for autonomous finance payment infrastructure The ledger must enforce four invariants by design before agents initiate payments: immutability, double-entry atomicity, idempotency by default, and regulatory-grade traceability at the posting level. 1. Immutability: append-only postings with compensating entries Every posting is written once, and agents correct errors by generating compensating postings that preserve history. A production-grade ledger should make transactions append-only. Corrections preserve lineage through compensating entries, so the past state can be reconstructed by replaying events. Overwriting destroys the lineage because, if a balance is wrong, a mutable ledger gives you no way to reconstruct the sequence of events that produced the error, and regulatory reconstruction of an agent's actions becomes impossible. 2. Double-entry atomicity across agent steps Atomic double-entry posting must debit and credit every autonomous fund movement in a single operation, so no partial posting can leave the ledger inconsistent between agent steps. Double-entry makes the invariant plain: money always has a source and a destination, and the ledger enforces accounting invariants internally. Retrofitting double-entry accounting later can become a multi-year engineering effort. 3. Idempotency by default for agent retries Idempotent API contracts make every payment operation safe by design. An agent retrying a timed-out call produces an identical ledger state across retries. The API contract must carry idempotency for the calling agent. The caller supplies a stable request identifier, and retries resolve to the same posting. If a deduplication key's retention window has lapsed within the client's retry window, the same operation can be processed again. An agent generating a fresh key on each replay defeats deduplication entirely. In a production ledger, double-entry atomicity should be a structural invariant enforced at the ledger layer, and a tamper-evident log should enforce immutability by default. For the surrounding payment API, idempotency at the API boundary means retries resolve to a single transaction. 4. Regulatory-grade traceability at the posting level Posting-level traceability requires every ledger posting to record the agent identity and authorization scope at posting time, along with a bi-temporal timestamp that tracks both when an event was recorded and when it was effective. Traceability must live in postings because application logs are rotated, filtered, and reformatted, so postings remain the system of record. An auditor or regulator may ask which agent initiated a transaction, under what authorization, and based on what state of the ledger. The answer has to come from the posting itself. How a core ledger records an autonomous finance payment A core ledger converts an agent's payment instruction into an immutable, double-entry posting as the single system of record. If the ledger cannot express the agent's intent precisely, the action is permanently opaque to regulators, auditors, and your finance team, because no upstream artifact survives with the same durability. Numscript , a purpose-built language for describing financial transactions, models the intent directly. The Formance Ledger is asset-agnostic because it tracks any asset the customer defines, including fiat currencies, stablecoins such as USDC and USDT, native crypto, custom tokens, and reward points. Below is a ledger model for the internal record of an autonomous stablecoin-to-fiat settlement coordinated through an external provider via Connectivity, the Formance module that handles integrations with PSPs, banks, exchanges, and custodians. The accounts are @platform:treasury, where the platform treasury holds funds the agent is authorized to move, and @platform:settlement:clearing, the internal settlement-clearing account. The multi-segment account path (platform:settlement:clearing) is a native Formance primitive that supports aggregation and querying without a schema migration. The initiating agent is recorded as transaction metadata: // AUTONOMOUS_SETTLEMENT_CLEARING // Event: treasury agent moves 2,500 USDC into settlement clearing send [USDC/6 2500000000] ( source = @platform:treasury destination = @platform:settlement:clearing ) set_tx_meta ( "event_type" , "autonomous_settlement_clearing" ) set_tx_meta ( "settlement_id" , "stl001" ) set_tx_meta ( "agent_id" , "treasury-agent-041" ) The send statement records 2,500 USDC (to six decimal places) in a single atomic posting; Numscript execution commits all modeled postings, or none. Actual conversion and fiat settlement would be initiated through a connected provider outside the Formance Ledger, orchestrated via Connectivity. The set_tx_meta calls bind treasury-agent-041 and stl001 to the transaction itself, so attribution queries run against the ledger even after application logs have been rotated or purged. Governance and Know-Your-Agent requirements for autonomous finance Oversight for agents that issue thousands of instructions per hour requires infrastructure that exposes every agent action as queryable, immutable, structured data in real time. Regulatory and fraud-control questions around agentic AI in finance are also drawing attention. The IMF frames this as a shift toward Know-Your-Agent requirements , where financial bot identities link to legal entities. For teams settling in stablecoins, GENIUS in the USA and MiCA in the European Union add specific reporting obligations that the ledger has to support without custom instrumentation. At the ledger layer, Know Your Agent starts with a stable identity for every payment-initiating agent, plus a scoped authorization envelope and transaction record that live where attribution queries can run against them. You have to distinguish the agent's own identity from delegated authority and scoped permissions, and each of those grants becomes a verifiable fact in the ledger. Real-time observability rests on bi-temporal recording. Effective time and recorded time together answer both what was true at a given moment and what the system knew at that moment. Bi-temporal recording supports point-in-time reconstruction of an agent's ordered actions without relying on mutable records. How to audit payment infrastructure before deploying AI agents Run the four invariants as a checklist against your current ledger before granting any autonomous agent payment-initiation rights: immutability, double-entry atomicity, idempotency by default, and posting-level traceability. In internally built systems, idempotency and attribution are the two most likely to be missing, because both tend to live in application code. Consider a cross-border payments platform whose client-side deduplication key expired after 60 seconds while the agent's retry backoff stretched to 90 seconds. On the second attempt, the ledger treated the request as new and posted the settlement twice, and the attribution table (updated only on the first call) pointed both postings at the same agent action. If your ledger fails any of the four invariants, resolve that gap at the ledger layer before extending payment-initiation rights to an agent. Reconciliation cannot compensate for structural gaps once agent throughput exceeds human review cadence. The Formance platform provides programmable financial infrastructure built around an open-source core ledger for fiat and digital assets, deployable as a sidecar ledger alongside existing core banking systems. Because immutability, double-entry atomicity, and audit traceability are enforced at the ledger layer, an auditor asking who moved the funds can rely on the same guarantees every time, without reimplementing those accounting primitives in application code.

body_text: Ultra-processed foods have become a major part of modern diets because they are convenient, affordable, and widely available. However, many health experts encourage reducing their consumption and replacing them with more whole and minimally processed foods whenever possible. While eliminating ultra-processed foods completely may not be realistic, making gradual changes can significantly improve your overall eating habits. The good news is that reducing ultra-processed foods does not require a complete lifestyle transformation. Small, consistent adjustments often produce lasting results. Below are eight practical strategies that can help you eat fewer ultra-processed foods while maintaining a balanced and sustainable approach. 1. Eat More Whole Plant Foods One of the easiest ways to reduce ultra-processed foods is to increase your intake of whole plant foods. Fresh fruits, vegetables, nuts, seeds, popcorn, and roasted seaweed are nutritious alternatives to many packaged snacks. For families with young children, introducing a wide variety of fruits and vegetables early in life can help develop healthier eating habits. Older children may also become more willing to try new foods when they are offered in different preparations and without pressure. Adding a plate of sliced vegetables with hummus before dinner or keeping fresh fruit within easy reach can naturally reduce the desire for highly processed snacks. 2. Choose Quality Ingredients Within Your Budget Buying the highest quality ingredients you can reasonably afford often makes healthy meals more enjoyable. Seasonal produce usually offers better flavor and freshness, making it easier to enjoy whole foods without relying on processed alternatives. Farmers markets are one option when available, but grocery stores also provide quality fresh, frozen, and canned fruits and vegetables. Frozen produce is often picked and preserved at peak freshness, making it a practical and nutritious choice. Simple ingredients that taste good require less processing and fewer added ingredients to become satisfying meals. 3. Learn More About Where Food Comes From Understanding how food is produced can encourage healthier choices. Learning about ingredients, food labels, and cooking methods helps consumers recognize ultra-processed foods more easily. Families can also benefit from discussing how different foods make them feel. Paying attention to energy levels, digestion, and overall well-being after meals encourages mindful eating instead of focusing only on taste. Reading ingredient lists and becoming familiar with the characteristics of ultra-processed foods can make grocery shopping much easier over time. 4. Cook More Meals at Home Preparing meals at home is one of the most effective ways to reduce ultra-processed foods. Home cooking gives you greater control over ingredients, cooking methods, and portion sizes. You do not need advanced culinary skills to get started. Learning basic cooking techniques such as sautéing vegetables, roasting proteins, and preparing simple sauces can build confidence in the kitchen. Start by mastering a few reliable recipes that your family enjoys. As your confidence grows, cooking from scratch becomes faster and more enjoyable, making processed convenience foods less necessary. 5. Bake Your Own Snacks and Desserts Many packaged desserts and baked goods are highly processed. Making your own cookies, muffins, or brownies allows you to control the ingredients while still enjoying your favorite treats. Baking at home does not have to be complicated. Begin with simple recipes from trusted sources and carefully read the instructions before starting. Organizing your ingredients ahead of time can also make the process smoother. Homemade baked goods often provide the same enjoyment while reducing preservatives and unnecessary additives commonly found in commercially packaged products. 6. Make Healthy Cooking More Convenient Convenience is one of the biggest reasons people rely on ultra-processed foods. Making home cooking easier can help overcome this challenge. Build a pantry stocked with staple ingredients such as rice, beans, pasta, canned tomatoes, herbs, spices, and healthy cooking oils. Keeping these essentials available makes it easier to prepare meals without making extra trips to the store. Meal preparation also saves time. Cooking larger portions allows you to enjoy leftovers throughout the week or freeze meals for busy days when cooking is not practical. Having healthy options ready often reduces the temptation to choose processed convenience foods. 7. Prioritize Shared Mealtimes Eating meals together can support healthier eating habits while strengthening family relationships. Shared meals encourage conversation, reduce distractions, and create opportunities to enjoy home-cooked food. Family meals do not need to be elaborate. Even simple dinners or takeout enjoyed together without phones or other distractions can help establish positive routines around eating. Consistency matters more than perfection. Scheduling a few shared meals each week can create lasting habits that benefit both adults and children. 8. Focus on Progress Instead of Perfection Completely avoiding ultra-processed foods is difficult because they are deeply integrated into modern food systems. Busy work schedules, social events, travel, illness, and convenience often make processed foods the easiest option. Rather than aiming for perfection, focus on making better choices most of the time. Gradually replacing processed foods with whole foods can help your taste preferences shift naturally over time. Healthy eating is built through thousands of small decisions rather than a single dramatic change. Every healthier choice contributes to long-term improvements in overall diet quality. Final Thoughts Reducing ultra-processed foods is not about following strict rules or eliminating every packaged product from your kitchen. Instead, it is about creating sustainable habits that prioritize whole foods whenever possible. By eating more plants, cooking at home, choosing better ingredients, baking simple treats, preparing meals ahead of time, and focusing on consistency rather than perfection, you can gradually reduce your reliance on ultra-processed foods without feeling overwhelmed. Small improvements made consistently often have a greater impact than extreme diets that are difficult to maintain. A realistic and balanced approach is more likely to become a lasting lifestyle change. Disclaimer This article is intended for informational and educational purposes only and should not be considered medical, nutritional, or professional healthcare advice. Always consult a qualified healthcare provider or registered dietitian before making significant dietary or lifestyle changes, especially if you have existing medical conditions or specific nutritional needs. Source Tthe Guardian article, July 22, 2026.

title: Medchart Alternatives
summary: Compare the top Medchart alternatives for personal injury and mass tort firms, including how Codes Health delivers AI-powered medical record retrieval and analysis with complete records in a couple of weeks, not months.
body_text: When evaluating Medchart alternatives, the decision comes down to your firm's case volume, need for AI-powered analysis, and integration requirements. While Medchart has established itself in the medical record retrieval space, many personal injury and mass tort firms now seek alternatives that combine retrieval with intelligent analysis, reducing paralegal review time and the need for separate chronology work. title: 7 Best Answer Engine Optimization Tools for Dominating AI
summary: You have spent months getting a page into the top three organic spots for a major keyword. The content is well optimized. Backlinks are solid.
body_text: Introduction You have spent months getting a page into the top three organic spots for a major keyword. The content is well optimized. Backlinks are solid. And then an AI Overview pulls a different source for its answer. That snippet, sitting above every blue link on the results page, can feel like both a theft and a warning. A 2026 study shows 46% of citations in Google's AI Overviews come from the top 10 organic results, but a high rank alone does not lock in the citation. Answer engine optimization, or AEO, is the side of modern search work that fixes this gap. It does not chase the page ranking. It chases extractability, making sure an AI model finds your content the easiest source to quote inside its generated answer for a given query. Getting this right for 2026 means treating the zero-click result as the primary screen. Key Takeaways Before dissecting the specific tools, the bottom line is that AEO requires a fundamentally different technology stack from traditional SEO. You cannot optimize what you cannot measure, and traditional rank trackers are blind to AI citations. The following six points are the strategic anchors for building your AEO toolkit. Freemium diagnostics: Tools like the HubSpot AEO Grader offer immediate, zero-cost content diagnostics, turning AEO from theory into a personalized action plan. Enterprise monitoring: Platforms such as Profound provide competitive benchmarking that quantifies brand visibility and loss of presence in AI-generated answers over time. Citation-to-revenue gap: No current platform offers a fully validated, deterministic citations-to-revenue attribution model, making directional data and leading metrics your most reliable north star. Technical engine: Machine readability driven by FAQPage schema and explicit entity definitions is a non-negotiable technical foundation for AI extraction. Realistic targets: A 10-point improvement in AI citation rate is a realistic six-month target for brands making active generative engine optimization investments. 1. Siftly: The All-in-One Command Center for AEO Strategy and Benchmarking Siftly is purpose-built as a generative engine optimization (GEO) operating system, not a traditional SEO suite with a bolted-on AI feature. Its core value lies in unifying keyword discovery, content grading, and competitive intelligence within a single workflow that tracks how AI systems evaluate content across major conversational platforms. Decision Dimension Siftly Traditional SEO Platforms Primary Optimization Target AI answer engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews) Search engine results pages (SERPs) Competitive Analysis Benchmarking competitor citations across query types Tracking competitor keyword rankings Content Grading Focus Answer readiness and extractability by AI models Keyword density and page-level authority Pricing Structure Tiered (Starter at $299/mo, Scale at $599/mo, custom Enterprise) Varies widely; often suite-based with add-ons For marketing teams specifically, a Siftly deployment answers two urgent questions: how often does our brand appear in AI-generated responses today, and how does that visibility stack up against competitors? It measures something most analytics suites miss entirely: AI-referred clicks and directional visibility uplift from structured content optimizations. 2. Semrush: The SEO Heavyweight Expanding into AI Visibility Scoring Semrush has pointed its data infrastructure at a new target: measuring whether your domain shows up inside AI-generated snapshot responses, not just its position on the blue-link SERP. The platform now folds AI visibility scoring into the same subscription where teams already watch rankings, backlinks, and site health. For SEO teams that live inside Semrush daily, the appeal is practical rather than aspirational. You add an AI Overviews tracker to an existing dashboard instead of learning a separate tool. That lowers the friction enough that adoption actually happens, which is the real hurdle for most new metrics. The tracker tells you two things: whether a tracked keyword fires an AI Overview, and if your domain gets cited inside it. A page can own the number-one organic spot and still get passed over as a source. Semrush turns that gap into a number you can watch week over week, giving you something concrete to report and a reason to adjust your content. The catch is the price. Access to this feature requires the suite subscription, which starts above $500 a month. That puts it squarely in the budget of teams already committed to the Semrush ecosystem, not the dabbler testing AEO for the first time. 3. HubSpot AEO Grader: The Freemium On-Ramp for Instant Content Diagnostics The HubSpot AEO Grader is a free tool that turns the theory of answer engine optimization into a specific, scorable report for any URL you give it. It reads the page and assigns a score based on how easily an AI engine can pull out the main answers. Diagnostic criteria: The grader inspects specific on-page elements including answer formatting, paragraph structure, authority signals, and schema markup presence. Answer-first analysis: It evaluates whether the page's key questions are answered by a clean, declarative sentence that AI models can pull verbatim, or if the answer is buried deep in prose. Freemium access: This instant, no-login-required tool acts as a lead generation gateway, offering immediate value and demonstrating the gap between traditional page optimization and AI readability. Actionable report: The output is not a theoretical guide. It provides a prioritized list of structural changes, serving as an effective starting point for a content team's AEO journey. 4. Profound: The Enterprise Search Analytics Firm Measuring Brand Share of AI Voice Profound runs enterprise brand monitoring across multiple AI search engines and produces competitive share-of-voice reports. These are not simple mention counts. The system queries engines like ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews at scale to track brand presence over time. This tool shifts AEO from a content editing task to a strategic intelligence function. It quantifies whether your brand is winning or losing presence in AI answers and identifies which competitors are gaining citation share. Instead of optimizing a single page, you see the competitive dynamics across an entire market category. The platform captures the narrative AI engines construct about your industry, showing exactly which types of queries your competitors are capturing at your expense. Off-site corroboration becomes measurable here. Profound's tracking reveals whether your entity appears across the credible, independent sources that answer engines treat as authoritative validation. 5. BrightEdge Generative Parser: The Incumbent's Lens on AI-Driven Traffic Shifts BrightEdge's Generative Parser operates at the intersection of AI visibility and its measurable impact on organic traffic. Its core capability lies in showing data-driven marketing leaders not just where they are cited, but what that citation actually does to their click-through rates and overall traffic patterns. Research indicates that for informational queries, webpages with a presence in AI Overviews had 1.5 times as many clicks compared to pages excluded from those overviews. The Generative Parser helps teams directly pattern-match these statistical correlations, revealing whether an AI citation is cannibalizing your clicks or, alternatively, creating a net-new discovery path. This distinction is critical because a blanket assumption that AI Overviews only reduce traffic is inaccurate; the tool surfaces the specific scenarios where citations drive traffic rather than suppress it. For transactional queries specifically, the impact is even more dramatic. The platform allows you to segment this analysis by query intent, content type, and page, moving the conversation from a generalized panic about AI-driven traffic loss to a surgical strategy for capturing high-intent traffic where it still exists. 6. seoClarity AI Snippet Optimizer: The Technical SEO Toolkit for AI-Ready Schema seoClarity's AI Snippet Optimizer approaches answer engine optimization as a fundamentally technical discipline, placing entity optimization and precise schema implementation at the core of its toolkit. It provides the auditing and deployment framework an SEO needs to structure content for efficient machine extraction. Its platform focuses on ensuring that FAQPage and HowTo schema, the highest-impact markup types for AI overviews, are not just present but implemented with the specific granularity that answer engines parse. The tool audits your pages for the explicit, consistent entity terminology that prevents AI models from having to make probabilistic guesses about what a page covers. Pricing for the suite starts at approximately $500 per month, positioning it as an investment for teams where technical SEO is the driving force and where machine readability across large, complex site architectures is the primary challenge. 7. Surfer SEO: The Content Editor Pivoting from Text Scores to AI Answer Scores Surfer SEO has changed what it measures. For years, the tool told you if a page was semantically complete enough for a search crawler. Now it tells you if your writing can survive being extracted by an AI and spoken as an answer. The output is different. Surfer still surfaces related terms and gives you a content score calibrated against the current SERP, but it has added a new layer. It grades whether a section opens with a self-contained, quotable statement that an AI engine can lift and cite as a definitive response. AI search engines do not index content. They extract it, and Surfer's newer scoring module grades you on exactly that extractability. For anyone who writes inside a document editor, the feedback sits right there on the screen. Machine readability stops being something you audit after publishing and becomes a standard you meet while the cursor is still blinking. Conclusion The answer engine optimization tool market in 2026 has sorted itself into three tiers, and each one solves a different problem. HubSpot's free diagnostic gives any content team a way to see whether AEO is an issue for them without spending a dollar. It makes the problem concrete, so you can decide if it is worth your time. At the $300 to $600 monthly level, Siftly, seoClarity, and Surfer SEO handle the daily work. They cover keyword research tuned for AI engines, entity markup, content grading against models like Claude and Perplexity, and competitive monitoring. This is where you do the actual optimization. When you need to measure brand share of AI voice and connect citations to traffic and revenue, Profound and BrightEdge are the enterprise option. They run the kind of large-scale analytics that justify a dedicated budget. Your tool choice follows your AEO maturity. Start with a diagnostic to build fluency. Move to a specialized platform when you are ready to optimize systematically. Reach for enterprise intelligence when you need to defend a position you already own. Frequently Asked Questions What is answer engine optimization and how does it differ from traditional SEO? Answer engine optimization (AEO) prepares content for direct citation by AI systems like ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews. While traditional SEO focuses on ranking full pages in organic search results through topic clusters, backlinks, and metadata, AEO structures content into extractable passages so answer engines can pull verbatim, self-contained answers. Content teams need both because AI engines highlight short answers while search engines continue to evaluate full pages for organic ranking. How do AI answer engines like ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews select and cite sources? Google's AI Overviews select sources primarily from its existing search index, with 46% of its citations originating from the top 10 organic results. Answer engines extract passages rather than ranking entire pages, preferring content that opens with a clean, declarative sentence answering a specific question. Off-site corroboration, where a brand appears consistently across independent credible sources, acts as an equally strong trust signal as any on-page factor. What metrics and KPIs matter for measuring GEO performance and ROI? AEO measurement involves a mix of metrics at different stages of the process: AI citation frequency: how often a domain appears as a cited source in AI-generated answers Zero-click visibility: whether a brand appears in generated answers that users see without clicking through Content grading scores: actionable leading indicators that measure extractability readiness Schema implementation rates: the percentage of pages properly structured with schema markup AI-referred traffic: the key outcome metric showing actual visits driven from AI citations Which content and schema strategies have the highest impact on AI citation rates? FAQPage and HowTo schema are the highest-impact structured data types for AI Overviews. However, the most impactful content strategy remains leading a page section with a single, clean declarative sentence that directly answers the section's question. This answer-first formatting, combined with consistent entity terminology and clear definitions that eliminate the need for AI inference, is proven to increase extraction rates more effectively than any other single on-page optimization. How can marketing teams track brand visibility and competitor benchmarks across AI platforms? Teams can use enterprise analytics platforms like Profound to query multiple AI engines at scale, tracking how often a brand appears in responses and generating competitive share-of-voice reports. Purpose-built GEO tools such as Siftly offer direct competitor citation monitoring that benchmarks visibility against rivals across specific query types, providing a clear directional snapshot of whether a brand is winning or losing presence in AI-generated answers over time. What tools and pricing models exist for answer engine optimization in 2026? The AEO tool market spans three pricing tiers: Freemium diagnostics: zero-cost, instant content reports from tools like the HubSpot AEO Grader Mid-range subscriptions: specialized GEO platforms such as Siftly at ~$300/month, and technical SEO suites like seoClarity and Semrush starting near $500/month Enterprise solutions: custom-priced monitoring from Profound and correlative analytics from BrightEdge, typically starting from $2,000/month Sources Answer Engine Optimization (AEO): The 2026 Guide - siftly.ai Answer engine optimization vs. traditional SEO - blog.hubspot.com Answer engine optimization: 6 AI models you should optimize for - searchengineland.com Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) vs SEO: What Changed? - Visible Factors - visiblefactors.com
